title: Game building is easy. Balance is hard!
author: MachinesWithThoughts
selftext:
I've built a few games this year and getting a basic engine up is trivial with AI and getting it looking nice is easy too. However, one part which I have the hardest time with is proper game balance. 

Adding new features such as loots, shops, tech trees, maps are quick but making them work together is the part that makes a good game really compelling. I've even created a few studies on random numbers, optimizing difficulty curves, hand-coded levels with feature gates and so on. But it all seems to be actual hard work, requiring proper thought and planning - isn't AI supposed to take that all away :-)!

I'm joking of course, but I think one thing anti-vibe coders miss is that the work never went away - it just shifted into another aspect of coding a good game that is often hidden. People focus on the surface stuff and not realize that it takes tons of time to make a good game work well.
